text:
maya: Customer support ticket #12578 — reports duplicate side-effects (emails sent twice / double billing) when assistant invokes email tool. They say it happened intermittently after a 202 Accepted from our API.

leo: Can you paste the request/response traces and any client retry behavior?

maya: Pasting minimal trace from customer reproduced locally: 

maya: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "model": "rwd-ig-1", "input": "send_email", "tools": ["email.send"], "idempotency_key": null }'
```

maya: Server responded with HTTP 202 and body {accepted: true, request_id: \"r-abc123\"}. Client retried after 3s and ended up with two tool executions.

sam: Can we pull the server-side function-invoke logs for request_id r-abc123? Suspect idempotency not applied on the queue path.

leo: Pulling logs now. Observed behavior: the model first attempted a toolcall but we returned a 400 schema validation (arg types wrong). The model then fell back to producing an assistant message and re-issued a corrected toolcall payload. The second toolcall was queued without an idempotency header. Separately, the client retried after the 202 and generated another run. End result: three tool-invokes recorded in the traces (two real executes).

emily: Customer code sample doesn't set an Idempotency-Key — they expected platform-level dedupe on 202.

raj: SRE note: our current 202 handling accepts and returns request_id but doesn't attach a persistent run-level dedupe key to the async queue item unless the client provided Idempotency-Key. If the model flow creates a new toolcall message (new call_id) we treat it as distinct.

maya: Repro steps I'm using: 
1)  Send a generate request that causes the model to produce an initial `tool_call` with invalid schema.
2) Model falls back and issues a corrected `tool_call` (new call) without reusing the earlier call_id.
3) Client receives 202 and retries once.

maya: Here's a short server log excerpt: 
```
[2024-01-10T14:21:02Z] request r-abc123 accepted status=202
[2024-01-10T14:21:05Z] tool.invoke start run=run-556 tool=email.send args={\"to\":\"user@example.com\",\"body\":\"...\"}
[2024-01-10T14:21:05Z] tool.invoke complete run=run-556 status=200
[2024-01-10T14:21:06Z] tool.invoke start run=run-557 tool=email.send args={\"to\":\"user@example.com\",\"body\":\"...\"}
[2024-01-10T14:21:06Z] tool.invoke complete run=run-557 status=200
```

leo: So root cause is threefold: (A) model fallback flow creates distinct toolcalls instead of updating prior call, (B) no generated idempotency token attached at accept-time, (C) client retries on 202. Combined they produced duplicate execution + billing.

sam: Immediate mitigation ideas: 
- On accept (202) generate a platform idempotency token tied to request_id and persist it on the async queue item. Reject duplicate tool.invoke attempts within short window if same request_id+tool_name+args fingerprint seen.
- Add an advisory to SDKs to auto-set Idempotency-Key on user requests.

leo: Long term: require tool-call schemas include stable call_id / call_signature so model can reuse corrected calls rather than create brand new ones. Also add a model-eval test that simulates fallback path.

emily: Customer needs refund + audit logs for which addresses were emailed and timestamps.

maya: Action items: 
- support: issue refund and send audit excerpt to customer (maya)
- eng-platform: patch dedupe-on-accept within 24h and add short-term guard (leo + sam)
- eng-runtime: add model-eval for fallback tool-call path (sam)
- sre: monitor for similar incidents and increase alerting on duplicate tool.exec events (raj)

leo: I'll open a small PR for the accept-time dedupe token and ping @sam for quick review :pray: 

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026 created (P2) — assigned to eng-platform.

sam: Noted. I'll add a unit test that reproduces a fallback -> retry sequence.

maya: Thanks everyone — I'll update the customer with ETA and steps. :thumbsup:
